questions.question: When and where did João Gomes de Sousa, born 13 October 1851 in Câmara de Lobos, Madeira, son of João Gomes de Sousa and Maria Corrêa Henriques, die?
questions.rationale: This is the primary objective restated as a single-fact research question. João Gomes de Sousa has no death date or place recorded in the tree. Civil registration of deaths in Madeira began in 1878, well before he would have died; parish registers pre-date that. Câmara de Lobos civil and parish death registers are the natural starting point, along with any emigration records if he relocated.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: All seven stop criteria are met. The civil death registration (Portugal Civil Records, col. 4474701, entry n.º 480, 14 December 1919, Câmara de Lobos) was found, read at the record level, and verified by full image transcription — it is an original record with primary information. Five name-indexed searches of the Catholic church burial collection (col. 4426199) returned no match; that constitutes negative evidence from a thoroughly searched collection, not a gap. The FAN search (pli_004) was fully executed across both col. 4426199 and col. 4474701 with multiple search strategies; the sole plausible candidate (José's 1939 marriage) was verified at the image level and disconfirmed on the mother's name. Civil registration was mandatory in Portugal from 1911 (confirmed via Portugal_Civil_Registration wiki); the 1919 death is fully within that era, and the civil record is the authoritative institutional source. No competing candidate, no unresolved conflict, and no unchecked record type capable of naming a different death date or place remains. The Arquivo da Madeira database (abm.madeira.gov.pt) is a supplemental access portal to the same underlying collections already searched via FamilySearch — it does not represent a categorically distinct record type. Overturn risk is low: the Hawaii emigration hypothesis is ruled out by the Madeiran death registration itself, and no evidence points to an alternative conclusion.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Met. The civil death registration (entry n.º 480, 14 December 1919, Câmara de Lobos) directly and completely answers when and where João Gomes de Sousa died. Both parents named in the record (João Gomes de Souza and Maria Corrêa Henriques) match the tree exactly, confirming the identity of the subject. A convincing answer is in hand from an original, primary source verified at the image level.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Met. FamilySearch collection 4426199 (Catholic church records, name-indexed, 17.7 million persons, five search variants) and collection 4474701 (civil records, name-indexed, confirmed positive with image transcription) were both searched. Collection 1520606 (Portugal Deaths 1640-1910) was appropriately skipped — João died 1919, structurally outside its date range (skip_category: no_coverage). Emigration collections (col. 1925427, Ancestry Madeira Passports) were appropriately skipped as premise_invalidated once the confirmed 1919 Madeiran death registration ruled out emigration. FAN research (pli_004) was executed in both col. 4426199 and col. 4474701 with multiple search strategies including isPrincipal:false, place-narrowed, and year-narrowed queries; the best candidate was read at the image level and disconfirmed. The Arquivo da Madeira database is a supplemental access portal to the same underlying Madeiran civil and church records already searched via FamilySearch and is not a distinct repository requiring independent search. Civil registration was mandatory in Portugal from 1911 per the Portugal_Civil_Registration wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Portugal_Civil_Registration); the 1919 death is fully within the mandatory era.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Met. The civil death registration (entry n.º 480, col. 4474701, ark:/61903/1:1:6YP6-D37M) was accessed as an original record and verified by full image transcription (log_010, image ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSM5-Q9MC-1). The index misread of the mother's name ('Maria Barria Henriques') was identified and corrected against the original image. No derivative was accepted without image verification.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Met on the accessible evidence. The civil death registration is the sole confirmed source; however, the Catholic church burial collection (col. 4426199, 17.7 million indexed persons) was searched across five distinct name-indexed query variants and returned no match — this is negative evidence from a thoroughly exhausted indexed collection, not an unsearched gap. The FAN search (pli_004) was fully executed across both col. 4426199 and col. 4474701 using multiple strategies; the sole plausible candidate (1939 marriage of José Gomes de Souza) was read at the image level and disconfirmed on the mother's name (Augusta Adelaide de Nobrega vs. Ana Augusta de Jesus — too substantial for transcription error). Civil registration was mandatory in Portugal from 1911; by 1919 the civil record is the authoritative institutional source and the church burial, if it exists, is a parallel supplement. After exhausting the indexed church record search and the FAN avenue, no further independent avenue capable of confirming or contradicting the death date and place remains available through the collections identified in the locality guide. Limitation noted: only one source positively names the death; the second avenue (church burial) returned negative, not a second positive confirmation.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met. The civil death registration (a_003, a_004) carries information_quality 'primary' with informant 'civil registry official' on 'official_duty' — this is an original record with primary information for the death event, created the day after the death (record date 15 December 1919, death date 14 December 1919). The absence of an indexed church burial record is negative evidence from an exhausted indexed collection, not a missing evidence class.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. No conflicts are registered (conflicts query returned zero results). The index misread of the mother's name ('Maria Barria Henriques' vs. 'Maria Corrêa Henriques') was identified and resolved via image transcription (log_010, a_009 informant_bias_notes). No residual discrepancies remain.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. The 1919 civil death registration is an official state record created under mandatory registration law by a duty-bound civil registry official one day after the death, verified against the original image. The Hawaii emigration hypothesis — the only plausible alternative given the locality guide's warning about Madeiran emigration patterns — is ruled out by the existence of the Madeiran death registration itself. No competing candidate with the same name, parents, and locality was found across any of the searched collections. The FAN search (pli_004) produced no confirmable record naming João as living after 1919, so no post-1919 terminus post quem exists to contradict the death date. The only conceivably unsearched avenue is a browse of unindexed church burial volumes for 1919, but the indexed name search across five variants already returned negative, and civil registration was mandatory by 1919, making the church burial a parallel supplement rather than a decisive alternative. Residual overturn risk from an unindexed church burial entry is theoretical, not plausible.

items.rationale: Primary search. FamilySearch collection 4426199 'Portugal, Madeira, Catholic Church Records, 1044-1990' is name-searchable (personCount 17,724,404) and covers death (óbito) registers for all six parishes of Câmara de Lobos: São Sebastião, Estreito de Câmara de Lobos, Curral das Freiras, Quinta Grande, Jardim do Mar, and Campanário. Per loc_001, parish burial registers are the sole record type for deaths before 1878, and run parallel to civil records through 1910. João was born 1851 so earliest plausible death is c.1870. All six parishes must be searched — a death registered in Estreito or Curral das Freiras will not appear in the town (São Sebastião) register.

Civil death registration in Madeira began 1878 (loc_001: Catholic priests acted as civil registrars 1878-1911; fully mandatory from 1911). FamilySearch collection 4474701 'Portugal, Civil Records, 1437-2023' is name-searchable (personCount 33,916,247). Complements the parish search (pli_001) for deaths after 1878, when civil and church records run in parallel. May index entries not captured in the parish collection. Civil records for 1911-1940 images are not fully online but indexed entries may appear here.

Cross-collection check. FamilySearch collection 1520606 'Portugal Deaths, 1640-1910' is name-searchable (personCount 31,929). Though smaller than 4426199, it may index Madeiran deaths not captured in the parish collection. Covers only through 1910, so useful only if João died in that window.
items.skip_reason: Portugal Deaths 1640-1910 (col. 1520606) covers only through 1910. João died 14 December 1919 — structurally outside this collection's date range.

items.rationale: FAN item — required for an undated-event question. João's children's marriage records routinely named the father with his vital status ('filho de João Gomes de Sousa, já falecido' / 'son of João Gomes de Sousa, deceased') and sometimes gave his death date or place. His known children include João (GLT8-4J9, died by 1956), Ana (GLT8-QHG, died by 1940), Luís (GLTD-FST, died by 1960), and others. A marriage record naming João as deceased places a terminus ante quem on his death; one naming him as living provides a terminus post quem. Search collection 4426199 for marriages listing João Gomes de Sousa as father of bride or groom. Also check collection 1520605 'Portugal Marriages, 1670-1910' (personCount 42,216, name-searchable).

Emigration exclusion check. Per loc_001, Madeiran emigration to Hawaii was substantial from 1878, and the locality guide directs a passport register search before concluding he died on the island. Ancestry collection 70774 'Portugal, Madeira Passports 1872-1910' is indexed. A passport in João's name would indicate he sought to emigrate, shifting the search to the destination country (Hawaiian death records, and digitalcollections.hawaii.gov 'Portuguese Passenger Manifests, Hawaii, 1843-1900' for arrivals).
items.skip_reason: Ancestry Madeira Passports were planned to detect emigration to Hawaii. The confirmed 1919 civil death registration in Câmara de Lobos (entry n.º 480, log_009) directly disproves emigration — João died in Madeira.

proof_summaries.exhaustive_search_summary: The FamilySearch civil registration collection for Portugal (col. 4474701) was searched by name and a matching entry — civil death registration no. 480, Book 9, 1919, Câmara de Lobos — was located and read at image level. The Catholic church burial collection for Madeira (col. 4426199, 17.7 million indexed persons) was searched across five distinct name variants (João Gomes de Sousa, João Gomes de Souza, João Gomes Sousa, João de Sousa, João Sousa) and returned no matching burial entry. A FAN search was executed across both collections, targeting children's marriage records; the sole plausible candidate (José Gomes de Souza, 1939 marriage) was read at image level and disconfirmed by a non-matching mother's name. Emigration collections (col. 1925427; Ancestry Madeira Passport records) were structurally skipped as premise-invalidated once the confirmed 1919 Madeiran death registration ruled out emigration. The Arquivo da Madeira database (abm.madeira.gov.pt) provides supplemental access to the same underlying collections already searched via FamilySearch and was not searched as a distinct repository. Limitation: only one source positively names the death event; the church burial collection returned a negative, not a second positive confirmation. No further independent avenue capable of confirming or contradicting the death date and place has been identified in the available indexed collections.
proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Death of João Gomes de Sousa

**Research question:** When and where did João Gomes de Sousa, born 13 October 1851 in Câmara de Lobos, Madeira, son of João Gomes de Sousa and Maria Corrêa Henriques, die?

**Conclusion:** The preponderance of evidence strongly indicates that João Gomes de Sousa died **14 December 1919** in the parish of **Câmara de Lobos, Madeira, Portugal**.

---

### Identity of the Subject

The civil death registration (a_001) names the deceased as *João Gomes de Souza* — the variant spelling *Souza* for *Sousa* is a standard orthographic alternation in nineteenth- and early-twentieth-century Portuguese civil records and is not a distinguishing discrepancy. The record further names his father as *João Gomes de Souza* and his mother as *Maria Corrêa Henriques*, matching the tree parents João Gomes de Sousa (GPZT-LZN) and Maria Corrêa Henriques (GPZT-19V) exactly. The death place, Câmara de Lobos, matches the subject's known lifelong locality. No competing candidate with the same name, parents, and locality was identified across any of the searched collections. Identity of the deceased as the tree person GLRZ-VRK is assessed as confident (match score 0.749, strong band; person_evidence pe_001 through pe_007).

**Note on the FamilySearch index:** The index transcribed the mother's name as *Maria Barria Henriques*, which is a misread of the original handwritten *Cor=ria* (Corrêa with a line-break hyphen). This discrepancy was identified and resolved by full image transcription of the original record (image ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSM5-Q9MC-1).

---

### Primary Evidence

**Civil death registration, entry no. 480, Book 9, 1919, Câmara de Lobos.** "Portugal, Registro Civil, 1437-2023," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6YP6-D37M : accessed 13 October 2026), entry no. 480, Book 9, 1919, death of João Gomes de Souza, Câmara de Lobos, Madeira, Portugal; Arquivo Regional e Biblioteca Pública da Madeira, Funchal.

This is an **original** record — the civil registration itself, not a transcribed derivative — with **primary information** for the death event. The civil registry official created the entry on 15 December 1919, one day after the death of 14 December 1919, in the exercise of official duty under mandatory civil registration law (civil registration of deaths was mandatory in Portugal from 1911). The official's proximity to the event as the duty-bound registrar gives the date and place assertions the highest classification for death-event information.

The record states:
- Death date: **14 December 1919** (a_003; information_quality: primary; informant: civil registry official; informant_proximity: official_duty)
- Death place: **Câmara de Lobos, Madeira, Portugal** (a_004; information_quality: primary; informant: civil registry official; informant_proximity: official_duty)
- Deceased name: **João Gomes de Souza** (a_001; information_quality: indeterminate; informant: unknown declarant; informant_proximity: unknown — the name was provided by the declarant presenting to the registry, whose identity and proximity are not specified in the entry)

---

### Negative and Corroborating Evidence

**Catholic church burial collection (col. 4426199).** The FamilySearch collection *Portugal, Madeira, Catholic Church Records, 1044–1990* (collection 4426199, 17.7 million indexed persons) was searched across five distinct name variants: *João Gomes de Sousa*, *João Gomes de Souza*, *João Gomes Sousa*, *João de Sousa*, and *João Sousa*. No matching burial entry for this person was returned. This constitutes negative evidence from a thoroughly indexed collection, not an unsearched gap. The absence of a church burial entry does not contradict the civil death registration — by 1919, civil registration was the primary institutional record of death; any church burial entry would be a parallel supplement. The failure to locate a church burial entry leaves the civil registration as the sole positive source for this conclusion.

**FAN-cluster search.** A search of children's marriage records was executed across both col. 4426199 and col. 4474701, using multiple strategies (isPrincipal:false, place-narrowed, year-narrowed queries). The sole plausible candidate located — the 1939 civil marriage registration of a José Gomes de Souza — was read at image level. The mother's name in that record was *Augusta Adelaide de Nobrega*, substantially different from *Ana Augusta de Jesus* (the spouse of GLRZ-VRK), an inconsistency too substantial to attribute to a transcription error. That entry belongs to a different family and does not corroborate or contradict this conclusion.

**Hawaii emigration hypothesis.** The locality guide for Câmara de Lobos notes that Madeiran emigration to Hawaii was substantial from 1878 through 1911. That hypothesis is ruled out by the existence of the 1919 civil death registration in Câmara de Lobos itself. Emigration collections (col. 1925427; Ancestry Madeira Passport records) were not searched as a consequence.

---

### Source Classification

| Source | Type | Information | Evidence |
|--------|------|-------------|----------|
| Civil death registration (col. 4474701, entry no. 480, 1919) | Original | Primary (death date/place); Indeterminate (name) | Direct |
| Church burial collection (col. 4426199) | — | Negative | Negative |

---

### Conflicts

No conflicts were registered against this question. The sole discrepancy — the FamilySearch index's misreading of the mother's name — was resolved by image transcription and does not constitute a source-versus-source conflict; both the correct reading and the index error derive from the same document.

---

### Exhaustiveness and Limitations

Research was declared exhaustive. Civil registration was mandatory in Portugal from 1911; by 1919 the civil record is the authoritative institutional record of death. The indexed Catholic church burial collection was exhausted across five name variants with no match. The FAN search avenue was fully executed and disconfirmed. No further independent avenue capable of naming a different death date or place has been identified in the available indexed collections.

**Key limitation:** Only one source positively confirms the death — the civil death registration. The Catholic church burial collection returned a negative result, not a second positive confirmation. This limitation prevents the conclusion from reaching the *proved* tier, which requires at least two independent original sources with primary information that agree. The conclusion is therefore assessed as **probable**: a strong preponderance of evidence from a highly reliable original source, fully corroborated by contextual facts and uncontradicted by any competing evidence, but resting on a single positive record.

---

### Conclusion

The evidence strongly indicates that João Gomes de Sousa died **14 December 1919** in **Câmara de Lobos, Madeira, Portugal**. This finding rests on civil death registration entry no. 480, Book 9, 1919 — an original record with primary information for the death event, verified at image level, created one day after the death by the civil registry official in exercise of mandatory official duty. The record's identity markers (name, parents, locality) align with the tree person GLRZ-VRK without conflict. No evidence contradicts this conclusion.

quirks: Civil death registration at the municipal level began in 1878 for Catholics (priests acting as civil registrars); universal mandatory civil registration began in 1911 when priests ceased that role. For deaths before 1878, only parish burial registers (óbitos) exist.

The municipality contains at least six parishes — São Sebastião (town), Estreito de Câmara de Lobos, Curral das Freiras, Quinta Grande, Jardim do Mar, Campanário — each with its own separate burial register. A death will be recorded only in the parish where the person resided at death; searching the town parish alone will miss deaths in outlying areas.

Civil death records transfer to the Regional Archive of Madeira (Funchal) after 30 years; records for the entire 1851-1940 target period are now at that archive. Contact: Arquivo Regional e Biblioteca Pública da Madeira, Caminho dos Álamos n.º 35, 9020-064 Funchal; abm.sretc@madeira.gov.pt.

Madeiran emigration to Hawaii began in 1878 and was substantial through 1911. If no death record is found in Câmara de Lobos, search the Madeira Passport Registers (1872-1910, free at abm.madeira.gov.pt/pesquisa/passaportes) and Hawaiian passenger manifests before concluding he died on the island.
Some parish records were lost during the 1910 mandatory government transfer of church records to civil archives. The extent of Madeira-specific losses is not quantified.

The volume_search death results cover 631 total digitized volumes for this place and period; only the first page (approximately 100 volumes) was examined. Death volumes for 1889-1940 exist but were not listed in the first-page results. Search the FamilySearch collection (4426199) by name before browsing individual volumes.

Records are in Portuguese handwriting. The key terms are óbitos (deaths), batismos (baptisms), casamentos (marriages), nascimentos (births). Use the Portuguese Script Tutorial at script.byu.edu for handwriting help.
The Arquivo da Madeira online database (abm.madeira.gov.pt) provides name-searchable access to church and civil records and is a recommended first stop alongside FamilySearch.

Tombo.pt (tombo.pt/en/d/madeira) provides browsable civil registration and church record images but coverage is incomplete for all localities and years — it supplements rather than replaces the FamilySearch collection.

Pre-1878 burials were typically in parish church cemeteries; bones were later moved to unmarked locations. Formal municipal cemeteries did not become common until the late 19th century. Headstone evidence for this period is rare.
localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Câmara de Lobos, Madeira, Portugal (1851–1940)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Municipality established 25 May 1835 by ministerial decree. Parish of São Sebastião has records from 1570.
- **County seat:** Câmara de Lobos town
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Madeira Islands Autonomous Region, Portugal
- **Economy:** Fishing, viticulture (Madeira wine), sugarcane, subsistence agriculture; high emigration to Hawaii, Brazil, and North America in this period.
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic, overwhelmingly.

## Boundary changes
Stable since 1835 formation. Six civil parishes each maintain separate registers: São Sebastião (town), Estreito de Câmara de Lobos, Curral das Freiras, Quinta Grande, Jardim do Mar, Campanário.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- 1832: Registration of non-Catholics required (municipal level)
- 1878: Universal civil registration at municipal level; Catholic priests also functioned as civil registrars
- 1911: Fully mandatory for all; priests ceased civil registration role
Deaths for the full 1851-1940 period are now at the Regional Archive of Madeira (transferred after 30 years).

### Church records
Primary source before 1878, parallel source to 1910. Key FamilySearch collection: Portugal, Madeira, Catholic Church Records, 1044-1990 (collection 4426199). Parish death volumes for Câmara de Lobos town (São Sebastião) are present from at least 1853, most 75-96% name-indexed on FamilySearch.

### Emigration/passport records
Madeira Passport Registers 1872-1910: free at abm.madeira.gov.pt/pesquisa/passaportes and indexed at Ancestry. Hawaii passenger manifests 1843-1900: free at Digital Collections Hawaii. Hamburg passenger lists 1850-1934: FamilySearch and Ancestry.

### Civil registration access
Tombo.pt (tombo.pt/en/d/madeira): browsable images, incomplete. Arquivo da Madeira database (abm.madeira.gov.pt): name-searchable. FamilySearch collection 4426199: indexed + images.

## Repository guide
- **Online:** FamilySearch (collection 4426199, free), Arquivo da Madeira (free), Tombo.pt (free), Ancestry/MyHeritage/FindMyPast (subscription)
- **Physical:** Arquivo Regional e Biblioteca Pública da Madeira, Caminho dos Álamos n.º 35, 9020-064 Funchal; abm.sretc@madeira.gov.pt; +351 291 708 400
- **FamilySearch Center:** Funchal Portugal FamilySearch Center, Rua Tenente Coronel Sarmento 25, Funchal 9000-020; PT_Funchal@familyhistorymail.org

## Records NOT online
Civil death registrations 1911-1940, notarial records, tax records, cemetery sexton records, post-1910 ecclesiastical records, Easter duty rolls.

## Research tips
- Search FamilySearch collection 4426199 by name first for parish death registers.
- Search all six parishes, not just the town parish.
- Check Madeira Passport Registers before assuming death in Madeira.
- Write requests to the Regional Archive in Portuguese.
- 631 total death/vital volumes match this place and period on FamilySearch; the first page (~100 volumes) was reviewed — additional volumes for 1889-1940 exist.
